note: Organelle / domain content + generation parameters. count = number rendered (reduced for legibility); realCount = literature scale. Sizes in the scene are exaggerated (see README). volumeFraction = share of hepatocyte volume (Alberts MBoC; Blouin 1977) where known.

cell.binucleateFraction: ≈25–30% of adult human hepatocytes are binucleate (verify; see UNCERTAINTIES.md)

items.name: Nucleus
items.realCount: 1 (≈25–30% of adult human hepatocytes are binucleate; many are polyploid)
items.function: Houses the genome; transcription of liver-specific genes (HNF4A, CEBPA…) and mRNA export through nuclear pores. Polyploid and binucleate hepatocytes are the norm in adult liver and confer stress resilience.
items.clinical: Glycogenated nuclei (diabetes, Wilson disease, MASLD); 'sanded' nuclei from HBcAg in chronic hepatitis B; nuclear pleomorphism and high N:C ratio in dysplasia and hepatocellular carcinoma.

items.name: Nucleolus
items.function: Site of rRNA synthesis and ribosome subunit assembly; large and active in hepatocytes because of their high protein-synthetic output.
items.clinical: Enlarged, prominent nucleoli are a feature of regenerating liver and of dysplastic or malignant hepatocytes.

items.name: Rough endoplasmic reticulum
items.sizeUm: cisternae ≈ 50–100 nm thick, stacked in basophilic clusters
items.function: Ribosome-studded cisternae synthesise secretory and membrane proteins (albumin, fibrinogen, clotting factors, apolipoproteins) and start N-glycosylation; ApoB100 is lipidated here by MTTP for VLDL assembly.
items.clinical: α1-antitrypsin deficiency (Z-polymers retained in RER); ground-glass hepatocytes from HBsAg accumulation; ER stress/unfolded-protein response in MASLD and alcohol-related liver disease.

items.name: Smooth endoplasmic reticulum
items.callout: Smooth ER (CYP450, UGT1A1, G6Pase, lipid synthesis)
items.function: Xenobiotic and steroid oxidation (CYP450), glucuronidation (UGT1A1 incl. bilirubin), glucose-6-phosphatase for glucose release, triglyceride and cholesterol synthesis, bile-acid synthesis (CYP7A1), Ca2+ storage.
items.clinical: Enzyme induction (rifampicin, phenobarbital) proliferates SER; Gilbert and Crigler–Najjar syndromes (UGT1A1); GSD Ia (G6PC1).

items.name: Golgi apparatus
items.callout: Golgi (glycan maturation, VLDL and protein secretion)
items.sizeUm: stacks of 4–6 cisternae; several per cell, pericanalicular
items.function: Processes and sorts secretory proteins and VLDL for exocytosis at the sinusoidal face; supplies apical (canalicular) transporters and lysosomal enzymes. Hepatocyte Golgi stacks cluster near the bile canaliculus.
items.clinical: Congenital disorders of glycosylation can present with liver disease and coagulopathy; disturbed trafficking of BSEP/MRP2 contributes to some cholestatic syndromes.

items.name: Mitochondrion
items.callout: Mitochondria (β-oxidation, TCA, OXPHOS, ketogenesis, urea cycle)
items.function: Fatty-acid β-oxidation, TCA cycle and oxidative phosphorylation; ketogenesis (HMGCS2); pyruvate carboxylase for gluconeogenesis; first two urea-cycle steps (CPS1, OTC); ATP for the cell's very high synthetic and transport workload.
items.clinical: Microvesicular steatosis with impaired β-oxidation (valproate, acute fatty liver of pregnancy, Reye); megamitochondria and reduced OXPHOS in alcohol-related and metabolic steatohepatitis; paracetamol toxicity involves mitochondrial injury.

items.name: Peroxisome
items.function: Very-long-chain fatty-acid and branched-chain oxidation, plasmalogen synthesis, H2O2 handling (catalase), and the final steps of bile-acid synthesis (side-chain shortening, amino-acid conjugation).
items.clinical: Zellweger spectrum disorders: hepatomegaly, cholestasis and fibrosis with VLCFA and bile-acid intermediate accumulation.

items.name: Lysosome
items.function: Degrades endocytosed lipoproteins (lysosomal acid lipase), autophagic cargo and damaged organelles; pericanalicular lysosomes also contribute to biliary secretion of some proteins and copper.
items.clinical: LAL deficiency (Wolman / CESD); Niemann–Pick C; lipofuscin accumulation with age; copper storage in Wilson disease.

items.name: Glycogen rosettes
items.sizeUm: α-particles ≈ 100–200 nm rosettes of ≈ 20–30 nm β-particles
items.function: Post-prandial glucose store (up to ≈5–8% of liver wet weight when fed), sited beside smooth ER; broken down by phosphorylase during fasting.
items.clinical: Glycogen storage diseases I, III, IV, VI, IX: hepatomegaly, hypoglycaemia; glycogenic hepatopathy in poorly controlled type 1 diabetes.

items.name: Lipid droplet
items.function: Neutral-lipid stores (triglyceride, cholesteryl ester) bounded by a phospholipid monolayer with PLIN2/5 coat; supply substrates for VLDL and β-oxidation.
items.clinical: Steatosis: ≥5% of hepatocytes with fat (MASLD). Macrovesicular (single large droplet displacing the nucleus) vs microvesicular. PNPLA3 I148M raises steatosis and fibrosis risk.

items.name: Sinusoidal (basolateral) membrane
items.function: Blood-facing domain, amplified about sixfold by microvilli. Houses uptake carriers (NTCP, OATP1B1/1B3, GLUT2, CD36) and is the site of secretory exocytosis (albumin, VLDL).
items.clinical: NTCP is the receptor for hepatitis B and D virus entry; sinusoidal uptake failure raises conjugated and unconjugated bile-acid and bilirubin levels.

items.name: Sinusoidal microvilli
items.callout: Microvilli project into the space of Disse
items.sizeUm: ≈0.1 µm wide, up to ≈0.5–1 µm long
items.function: Increase the exchange surface toward the plasma-filled space of Disse, allowing rapid uptake from albumin-bound ligands.
items.clinical: Microvilli are lost or blunted in cholestasis and injury; capillarisation and collagen deposition in the space of Disse impairs exchange in cirrhosis.

items.name: Canalicular (apical) membrane
items.function: Apical domain forming the bile canaliculus with short microvilli. Houses ATP-dependent efflux pumps (BSEP, MRP2, ABCG5/G8, P-gp, BCRP, ABCB4) that drive bile secretion.
items.clinical: PFIC1 (ATP8B1), PFIC2 (ABCB11), PFIC3 (ABCB4); Dubin–Johnson (ABCC2); raised ALP/GGT in cholestasis.

items.name: Bile canaliculus
items.callout: Bile canaliculus (≈1 µm lumen, sealed by tight junctions)
items.function: Tiny channel between adjacent hepatocytes that collects primary bile. Bile flows toward the periportal Canal of Hering, i.e. in the opposite direction to blood flow in the sinusoid.
items.clinical: Canalicular cholestasis: dilated canaliculi with bile plugs on histology; bile-duct obstruction raises intracanalicular pressure and disrupts tight junctions.

items.name: Lateral membrane
items.callout: Lateral domain (~50% of surface; neighbour contact)
items.function: Contact faces with neighbouring hepatocytes, carrying desmosomes and gap junctions and bounded apically by the tight junctions that seal the canaliculus.
items.clinical: Loss of lateral integrity in interface hepatitis and cholestasis.

items.name: Tight junction
items.function: Claudin/occludin/ZO-1 strands seal the canaliculus from the sinusoid and space of Disse and define the polarity border between apical and basolateral domains.
items.clinical: TJP2 deficiency (PFIC4) and claudin-1 defects (neonatal ichthyosis-sclerosing cholangitis) give cholestasis; leaky junctions allow bile regurgitation.

items.name: Space of Disse
items.function: Plasma-filled gap between LSEC and hepatocyte; no basement membrane, so albumin-bound ligands reach the microvilli directly. Hepatic stellate cells reside here.
items.clinical: Collagen deposition and loss of LSEC fenestrae (capillarisation) in fibrosis and cirrhosis; stellate-cell activation drives fibrosis.

items.name: Sinusoidal endothelium (LSEC)
items.sizeUm: fenestrae ≈ 100–200 nm, grouped in sieve plates
items.function: Fenestrated endothelium without a diaphragm or basement membrane filters chylomicron remnants, VLDL and plasma proteins in both directions; also scavenges waste macromolecules.
items.clinical: Capillarisation (fenestrae lost) in cirrhosis; LSEC injury in sinusoidal obstruction syndrome.

items.name: Sinusoid lumen
items.function: Low-pressure capillary carrying mixed portal-venous and hepatic-arterial blood past the hepatocyte plate, from portal tract to central vein.
items.clinical: Portal hypertension and sinusoidal resistance in cirrhosis; Budd–Chiari syndrome.
